concerns.text: FR-016 requires the pipeline to run on an environment with at least 4 CPU cores and 16 GB RAM (or a self‑hosted runner). T001’s verification only checks that the .env file loads; it does not enforce the required compute resources, nor does it prohibit the optional ‘Kaggle GPU’ path mentioned in the header. This weakens the compute‑feasibility constraint.

FR-007 mandates a manual verification set of ≥ 100 blocks with precision ≥ 0.85 and recall ≥ 0.85 (95 % CIs). T005 specifies the sample size and precision/recall thresholds, but it does not require reporting the confidence intervals, thereby dropping a required acceptance criterion.

FR-012 requires that every individual maintenance event (churn or bug‑fix) be persisted as a `MaintenanceEvent` record adhering to the schema. T007 extracts churn and latency metrics but never writes the per‑event JSON file, violating the functional requirement.

FR-009 (a‑priori power analysis) is absent from the task list. The spec demands an explicit power analysis that determines a minimum of 250 matched pairs before data collection. Its omission means the study proceeds without the required pre‑study power justification.

SC‑007 expects a concrete coverage proportion for matched pairs that have both churn and latency metrics (the placeholder “[deferred]” is not acceptable in a success criterion). T007 only extracts the metrics but does not verify or report the required proportion, leaving the success criterion untestable.

The header of the tasks file states that all tasks must run on the “default CPU‑first CI environment (or a Kaggle GPU only if absolutely required)”. Introducing a Kaggle GPU path creates a silent constitution drift (Principle III – Data Hygiene & Principle I – Reproducibility) because external compute resources are not part of the documented environment and may affect reproducibility.

SC‑008 requires that the direction and statistical significance be robust when comparing 3‑month vs 6‑month windows. T010 records the comparison but does not explicitly assert that conclusions are unchanged, nor does it flag a failure if they are. This drops a required verification step.
